newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seen resuming upward course.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seen resuming upward course.

text.p: Argentine stocks were seen building on recent gains at the opening Monday, dealers said.
"Stocks will be fuelled by the prevailing climate of enthusiasm seen in markets here and abroad," said Rodrigo Diz at brokers Velox Inversiones.
The bolsa's weighted MerVal index rose 1.5 percent last week to 850.62 and stands 5.1 percent higher in July.

"The market still looks good but this buying spree could be entering its final stages and may be fizzling towards the end of the week," Diz said. "I don't think the MerVal will manage to reach its target of 900 just yet."
Traders said local players would keep an eye on a slew of earnings reports due this week on Wall Street which could cause some volatility on U.S. markets.

"The Dow keeps flirting with the 8000 level but it's finding pretty stiff resistance," an analyst at a U.S. investment bank said. "That's why if earnings are even slightly below consensus estimates, stocks will suffer."

Traders said they were looking forward to this week's flotation of 10 percent of the share capital of bolsa bellwether YPF which had been awarded for purchase by employees when the company was sold in 1993.

"The sale may keep a lid on the price of the stock for a couple of days, but beyond that it's a good thing because it reduces uncertainty regarding possible sudden changes in large company stakes," Diz said.
